findings.title: Unsafe destructure of destinationCalendar causes TypeError when array is empty
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` on the next line. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is an empty array (no connected calendar for any host, which is a common and valid scenario), `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined`, and accessing `.integration` on it throws a TypeError whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType`. The previous code used optional chaining (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`) which safely handled the missing-calendar case and fell back to Cal Video. This regression will crash booking creation for any user who selects Google Meet as location but has no destination calendar connected.

findings.title: updateEvent/deleteEvent calendarId resolution is broken when externalCalendarId is falsy
findings.body: In `updateEvent` (and the identical pattern in `deleteEvent` at line ~315), the fallback is: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (undefined/null), this predicate compares each `cal.externalId` to the same falsy `externalCalendarId` value, which will basically never be true for any real calendar entry, so `.find()` returns `undefined` and `selectedCalendar`/`calendarId` end up `undefined`. The previous code simply fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, which correctly picked a default calendar. Now, any update or delete call made without an externalCalendarId (e.g. legacy bookings or calendar references lacking it) will be issued with `calendarId: undefined`, which will fail against the Google Calendar API or silently target the wrong calendar. This affects reschedule and cancellation flows broadly, not just the multi-host scenario the PR targets.

findings.title: Lark/Office365/CalDAV calendar services always use the first destinationCalendar entry regardless of the credential being processed
findings.body: `createEvent`, `createAttendees`, `updateEvent`, and `deleteEvent` all do `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and use that single entry as the calendar id, ignoring which specific host/credential each CalendarService instance represents. Unlike GoogleCalendarService (which was updated to match `destinationCalendar` entries by `credentialId`), Lark, Office365 (`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, line 73) and the generic CalDAV `BaseCalendarService` (`packages/lib/CalendarService.ts`, lines 156 and 509) were not updated the same way. In a collective event with multiple hosts using these calendar providers, the event will always be created/updated/deleted against the first host's calendar, even when processing the second (or later) host's credential — defeating the stated purpose of this PR for every non-Google calendar integration.

findings.title: destinationCalendar defaults to null, silently dropping team members' calendars for collective events
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized as `eventType.destinationCalendar ? [...] : organizerUser.destinationCalendar ? [...] : null` — note the `null` fallback instead of `[]`. Immediately after, for collective events the code does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. If the organizer has no personal destination calendar and the event type has none either, `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, so the optional-chained `.push(...)` becomes a no-op and all team members' destination calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded. This directly undermines the PR's goal of inviting every host with a calendar app to the event, specifically in the case where the organizer (first host) has no destination calendar configured but other hosts do.

findings.title: Inconsistent destinationCalendar fallback values (null vs []) across the codebase
findings.body: `handleNewBooking.ts` falls back to `null` when no destination calendar is available, whereas essentially every other call site touched by this PR (`handleCancelBooking.ts`, `confirm.handler.ts`, `editLocation.handler.ts`, `webhook.ts`, `paypal-webhook.ts`, `requestReschedule.handler.ts`, `deleteCredential.handler.ts`) falls back to `[]`. Since `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` is typed as `DestinationCalendar[] | null`, both are technically valid, but the inconsistency means downstream code and tests must handle two different 'empty' representations for the same conceptual state, increasing the risk of bugs like the `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)` no-op described separately, and making behavior harder to reason about/test consistently.

findings.title: No automated tests added for the core multi-destinationCalendar feature
findings.body: The PR description explicitly checks 'I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works'. The only test changes are a cosmetic update to `apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts` changing an expected payload field from `null` to `[]`, which does not exercise the actual multi-host/multi-destinationCalendar logic (array iteration in `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`/`updateAllCalendarEvents`, per-credential calendar matching in `GoogleCalendarService`, or the collective-event team calendar collection in `handleNewBooking.ts`). Given the extent and risk of the refactor (converting a singular field to an array across ~20 files), the lack of unit/integration coverage for the new array-handling paths is a significant gap that should block merging until at least basic coverage is added.
